papers.title: Deep history of an ancient subterranean crustacean: origins of the Bathynellacea (Syncarida).
papers.abstract: Plate-tectonic-mediated vicariance is often invoked to explain global disjunct distributions. However, since the advent of molecular tools, particularly molecular dating, it has become apparent that in many of the taxa, dispersal post-continental break-up better explains their current distribution. Nevertheless, these taxa belong to younger radiations and are less suitable for deep-time biogeographic studies. Here, we target an ancient lineage of subterranean freshwater crustacean of the order Bathynellacea with limited dispersal ability and global distributions to investigate the role of plate-tectonic-mediated vicariance. We investigated the evolutionary relationships among bathynellaceans using phylogenetic analyses of nuclear and mitochondrial markers. For the first time, four outgroup fossils were used to calibrate the time tree to date the origin and significant diversification events of bathynellaceans. Our results reveal deep phylogenetic divergences among Bathynellacean families, suggesting an ancient origin dating back to the Mesozoic or possibly even the Late Palaeozoic. The early branching lineages are geographically distributed across former Gondwanan landmasses and Eurasia, supporting a dual origin scenario and challenging previous views of a single Laurasian ancestry. The taxonomic implications of our phylogeny are also discussed. Overall, this study demonstrates Bathynellacea as a valuable model for understanding deep-time evolutionary processes.

papers.title: Synthesis and isolation of stable oxoboranes.
papers.abstract: Oxoboranes, molecules bearing a triple bond between a dicoordinate boron atom and a monocoordinate oxygen atom, are some of the longest-sought reactive main-group species. Their syntheses have been the subject of a series of documented attempts dating back to at least the early 1960s, leading to gas-phase/matrix isolation and evidence of chemical trapping, as well as isolation of oxoborane derivatives with reduced B-O bond orders. However, their detection or isolation of base-/acid-free oxoboranes in the condensed phase remains challenging. Here we present a remarkably simple synthesis of three oxoboranes that are stable as crystalline solids at room temperature. These species feature exceptionally short (1.208(4)-1.217(4) Å) and strong B-O bonds. Their properties are elucidated by both experimental and computational methods, and an explanation for their unusual stability is provided.

papers.title: ESR Essentials: "Gadolinium-free" pediatric neuroimaging-practice recommendations by the European Society of Neuroradiology.
papers.abstract: Gadolinium-based contrast agents (GBCA) have been central to magnetic resonance neuroimaging, enhancing diagnostic sensitivity and accuracy, in both adults and children. However, their increasingly widespread use has raised concerns, as evidence exists of gadolinium retention in brain tissue after repeated use. This paper outlines some updated strategies to reduce GBCA administration in pediatric neuroradiology, based on both recent literature and the authors' clinical experience. This paper, therefore, should be considered as a concise review of the main literature data and the opinion of a group of experts in the field, based on their daily practice in large institutions. We mention those most frequent conditions where the usage of GBCA often represents a longstanding, albeit "not strictly evidence-based," common practice which can be critically reconsidered. The use of GBCA in pediatric neuroimaging should be considered carefully based on each case scenario, evaluating if GBCA may provide real and substantial potential benefits to patient management and outcome. KEY POINTS: The use of GBCA in pediatric neuroimaging should be carefully evaluated by the pediatric neuroradiologist on an individual basis, and it should also be supported by specific literature data if present, so as to balance risks and benefits and to improve patient management and outcome. Possible alternative strategies to the use of GBCA may be considered in some cases under a close relationship between pediatric neuroradiologists and clinicians. Prospective development of new sequences is needed to improve unenhanced MR imaging accuracy and expand "Gd-free" examinations.

papers.title: Can maternal characteristics improve due date prediction without ultrasound? Development and internal validation of a machine-learning prediction model in 600 000 pregnancies in Sweden.
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT: To assess whether estimated due dates based on Naegele’s rule can be improved by incorporating routinely collected maternal characteristics into a non-parametric machine learning model, particularly in settings where ultrasound is unavailable. DESIGN: Population-based retrospective cohort study; development and internal validation of a machine-learning prediction model. SETTING: Nationwide register data from Sweden. PARTICIPANTS: 603 861 singleton pregnancies recorded in the Swedish Medical Birth Register between 2008 and 2017. We restricted the sample to spontaneous singleton births with complete information on last menstrual period, ultrasound dating and maternal characteristics and further limited the primary analysis to pregnancies in which both Naegele’s rule and ultrasound-based gestational age at delivery fell between 37 and 42 completed weeks. PRIMARY AND SECONDARY OUTCOME MEASURES: The primary outcome was prediction accuracy of the date of delivery. Performance was evaluated using exact-day accuracy, accuracy within ±1 and ±7 days, mean squared error and root mean squared error. Machine-learning predictions were compared with those obtained using Naegele’s rule and ultrasound-based dating under identical inclusion criteria. RESULTS: The machine-learning model improved prediction accuracy over Naegele’s rule across all evaluated measures, while ultrasound-based dating remained more accurate overall. The model reduced between 25% and 45% of the accuracy gap between Naegele’s rule and ultrasound. Subgroup-specific models provided little additional improvement. Among second-time mothers, however, adding gestational duration from the previous pregnancy yielded markedly greater gains and produced prediction accuracy comparable to, and on some measures slightly better than, ultrasound. CONCLUSIONS: Incorporating maternal characteristics into a regression-forest model improved due date pred

papers.title: Primary cilia mediate specific neuron-glia attachments in C. elegans through the secreted protein BUG-1.
papers.abstract: Primary cilia are signaling hubs that influence nearly every aspect of cell physiology. Neuronal primary cilia were recently found to form extensive attachments to glia in the mammalian brain, but it is not known how these attachments form or what functions they serve. Defects in cilia cause profound neurological disorders, highlighting the importance of understanding the specialized functions of neuronal cilia. Here, we use a genetic screen in Caenorhabditis elegans to determine how a stereotyped cilia-glia attachment forms and how the attachment affects ciliary calcium signaling. We find that two sensory neurons (URX and BAG) use their cilia to attach to a specific glial partner (ILsoL/R). This attachment requires BUG-1, a large secreted protein that localizes precisely to the cilia-glia attachment site. In the absence of BUG-1, neuronal cilia are present but always fail to attach to the glial cell. As a result, the URX cilia do not undergo activity-dependent remodeling seen in wild-type neurons and the BAG cilia exhibit reduced sensory stimulus-evoked calcium entry and defects in calcium clearance. Our work shows that cilia can select specific glial partners for attachment, identifies a novel protein that mediates these attachments, and demonstrates the functional consequences of loss of cilia-glia attachment on neuronal signaling. We propose that neuronal primary cilia act not only as antennae to receive long-range signals but also as points of close-range cell-cell contact, through which glia could modulate neuronal signaling.

papers.title: Redox-Active Verdazyl Radical Polymers via Postpolymerization Modification of Active Ester Polymers.
papers.abstract: Organic radical polymers (ORPs) are constructed with 1,5-dimethyl-6-oxoverdazyl radicals for assessment as redox-active materials. The ORPs were synthesized through the postpolymerization modification (PPM) of poly(pentafluorophenyl methacrylate) (P1) and poly(pentafluorophenyl acrylate) (P2) with either 1,5-dimethyl-3-(p-aniline)-6-oxoverdazyl (1), 1,5-dimethyl-3-(4-methylamine-(1,1'-biphenyl))-6-oxoverdazyl (2) or 1,5-dimethyl-3-(4-methylamine-(1,1'-biphenyl))-6-oxoverdazyl (3). To overcome the limited stability of 1, radicals containing bulky C3 substituents and alkyl spacers to the heteroatom of the 4-methylamine or 4-hydroxymethyl moiety were synthesized from high yielding (78%-98%) Suzuki-Miyaura cross-couplings. The large cell potential (E°cell(3) = 1.67 V) and radical stability ensure these are well suited to fundamental electrochemical proof of concept studies when incorporated into a polymer. Variable radical attachment (0%-75%) was observed in PPM reactions. The ester aminolysis of P2 yielded the highest radical containing polymer (P2-2; 75%). As a proof-of-concept electrochemical demonstration, P2-2 and P2-3 exhibited a reversible redox couple at 3.43 V (vs. Li/Li+), successfully validating the redox activity of the verdazyl-functionalized polymers in a coin cell.

papers.title: Quantum chemical studies of the infrared spectra of OCN- in water and icy matrices and their astrophysical implications.
papers.abstract: The interstellar 'XCN' band is a distinct infrared absorption feature observed at 4.62 micron in the spectra of interstellar ices. Previous studies indicate that OCN- is likely responsible for the 'XCN' feature due to its correlations with other ice species observed in many astronomical sources. Yet, questions remain about the exact conditions and environments in which OCN- produces the 'XCN' feature. In this study we use computational chemistry methods to better understand the specific environments in which OCN- could produce the observed 'XCN' feature. By applying ab initio quantum chemical methods, such as density functional theory (DFT) and molecular dynamics, we explore the vibrational properties of OCN- under various conditions. Our approach involves computationally modeling OCN- in conditions representative of interstellar ice, considering the potential interactions with common ice constituents. We find that a coupled and structured hydrogen bonding network around the nitrogen atom of OCN- is responsible for the significant shift in the CN stretching frequency from gas phase to condensed phase. The computational vibrational data and spectra generated here with state-of-the-art ab initio quantum chemistry and molecular dynamics methods, combined with fresh experimental data, conclusively prove that OCN- embedded in water ice can fully account for the 4.62 micron astronomical 'XCN' feature. This computational investigation also establishes that while ammonium or other counter-ions may contribute towards local charge neutrality, they are not required to explain the position of the CN stretching band that appears near 2165 cm-1. The results of this study provide a new perspective on the molecular processes at play in interstellar ices and offer a solid foundation to interpret the 'XCN' feature. This research contributes to a broader effort to interpret astronomical observations of interstellar environments and advance our knowledge of astrochemical processes.

papers.title: Poorer bereavement outcomes among companion animal owners are associated with unexpected death or describing the pet as a partner or soulmate.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To examine whether circumstances surrounding companion animal death and the owner-companion animal relationship were associated with bereavement outcomes. METHODS: Cross-sectional survey data from 4,902 bereaved companion animal owners were analyzed. Multivariable regression models examined associations of cause of death, euthanasia, presence at death, and owner-reported relationship with the companion animal with grief severity, severe depression, anxiety/insomnia, social dysfunction, and somatic symptoms, adjusting for pet attachment and demographic and loss-related characteristics. Model sample sizes ranged from 4,099 to 4,758. RESULTS: Unexpected death, compared with natural or anticipated death, was associated with greater grief (unstandardized regression coefficient [B] = 2.49; 95% CI, 1.81 to 3.18), severe depression (B = 1.16; 95% CI, 0.59 to 1.73), anxiety/insomnia (B = 0.84; 95% CI, 0.32 to 1.35), social dysfunction (B = 0.97; 95% CI, 0.56 to 1.37), and somatic symptoms (B = 0.48; 95% CI, 0.02 to 0.94). Describing the companion animal as a partner or soulmate versus a best friend was also associated with poorer outcomes across all 5 domains (B = 0.60 to 1.26). Euthanasia was associated with lower grief (B = -0.95; 95% CI, -1.46 to -0.44) and depression (B = -0.76; 95% CI, -1.19 to -0.32). Presence at death was not associated with any outcome. CONCLUSIONS: Unexpected death and a partner/soulmate relationship were consistently associated with poorer bereavement outcomes. CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Veterinary practices should strive to ensure that owners experiencing an unexpected loss receive the same opportunities for follow-up and bereavement support as those whose companion animals undergo euthanasia.

papers.title: Charge collection efficiency in air-vented plane-parallel ionisation chambers at ultra-high dose rates: a self-consistent Garfield++ Monte Carlo model including space-charge effects and ion recombination.
papers.abstract: Ultra-high dose rate (UHDR) irradiation used in FLASH radiotherapy can lead to significant reductions in charge collection efficiency (CCE) in plane-parallel ionisation chambers (PPICs) due to enhanced ion recombination, while the high charge densities involved can also induce strong space-charge-induced electric-field distortions. This work aims to develop a Monte Carlo framework for investigating these coupled effects.&#xD;&#xD;Approach: We extended the Garfield++ Monte Carlo particle-transport framework by implementing ion-ion recombination and self-consistent space-charge electric field calculations. The resulting model couples particle transport, electron attachment, recombination processes, and dynamic electric-field distortions. The implementation was validated against analytical and numerical models from the literature.&#xD;&#xD;Main results: Excellent agreement was obtained for the free electron fraction (FEF), CCE, induced current, and electric field evolution under UHDR conditions. The simulations show that space charge can locally increase the electric field by more than a factor of four or reduce it to nearly zero in some regions of the chamber. The results further suggest that the decrease in the FEF caused by electric-field-dependent electron attachment plays a major role in the reduction of the CCE under UHDR conditions.&#xD;&#xD;Significance: These findings highlight the importance of accurately describing the evolution of the FEF for modelling recombination under UHDR conditions, opening up prospects for improved analytical models and real-time correction methods for ionisation chamber dosimetry. More broadly, this work provides a flexible and self-consistent Monte Carlo framework for investigating recombination phenomena and improving dosimetry models for FLASH radiotherapy.

papers.title: Study on road performance, microstructural evolution, and environmental safety of red mud-modified reactive cold-mix asphalt mixtures.
papers.abstract: Slow early-strength development limits the application of cold-mix asphalt (CMA), while environmental challenges of red mud (RM) utilization remain unresolved. This study developed RM-modified reactive cold-mix asphalt mixtures (RCMA) using reactive liquid asphalt (RLA), an alkali activator, and water to integrate organic curing with inorganic activation. The effects of RM on mechanical performance, microstructure, and environmental stability were investigated through multi-age tests, X-ray diffraction (XRD), X-ray fluorescence (XRF), scanning electron microscopy coupled with energy-dispersive spectroscopy (SEM-EDS), and leaching tests. Results showed that 30% reactive diluent (RD) and 5% RLA achieved workability and early-age stability. Compared with limestone powder (LP), RM improved high-temperature stability, low-temperature cracking resistance, and moisture durability, with residual stability (RS) close to or above 100% after water immersion. RM incorporation promoted a denser organic-inorganic structure by introducing Si-, Al-, and Fe-bearing reactive components and enhancing interfacial bonding. Leaching tests under thermal, ambient, and freeze-thaw conditions confirmed that regulated metals remained below limits, although Ni showed higher sensitivity. Enhanced performance was attributed to synergistic effects of moisture-triggered polyurea network and RM-derived reaction-product-rich regions, improving interfacial transition zone (ITZ) densification, stress transfer, and contaminant retention. This study provides a low-energy approach for RM utilization in sustainable pavement engineering.

papers.title: An attachment perspective on support and depressive symptoms in adult child-parent relationships.
papers.journal: Journal of family psychology : JFP : journal of the Division of Family Psychology of the American Psychological Association (Division 43)
papers.abstract: The adult child-parent relationship is a mutual support resource that promotes well-being across generations. This study takes a dyadic attachment perspective to examine how providing two attachment-based support processes, secure base and safe haven, is associated with one's own and their partner's depressive symptoms in older parents and adult children. A total of 128 adult child-parent dyads (Mparents' age = 69.63; Mchildren's age = 42.02) were recruited. Structural equation modeling was used to assess actor and partner associations of attachment-based support with depressive symptoms. For both generations, secure base provision was associated with lower actor, but not partner, depressive symptoms. Children's safe haven provision was associated with higher depressive symptoms in parents. Moderation analyses indicated that the association between parents' secure base provision and their own depressive symptoms was stronger at lower levels of children's secure base provision. For safe haven support, children's provision was positively associated with their own depressive symptoms only when parents' safe haven provision was low. Secure base provision may help parents maintain role continuity and resilience, associated with lower depressive symptoms. For adult children, providing a secure base may support a balance between responding to parental needs and maintaining personal goals and is associated with lower depressive symptoms. However, high levels of parental safe haven provision may place pressure on children to reciprocate, contributing to higher depressive symptoms. papers.title: Jealousy decreases as rival number increases: Preregistered tests differentiating between functional and intuitive views.
papers.abstract: Intuition and theory alike suggest that romantic jealousy should track the "amount" of cheating, with jealousy increasing as the number of affair partners increases. A functional account-conceptualizing romantic jealousy as an adaptation for managing the relationship-relevant fitness threats posed by romantic rivals-suggests instead that jealousy should track the implications entailed by infidelity. In this view, repeated infidelity involving a single affair partner may imply greater emotional involvement than the same number of encounters divided across multiple partners. We tested between these accounts using two preregistered studies of U.S.-residing CloudResearch participants (N = 1,318) conducted in 2023. In Experiment 1, using a repeated-measures design, jealousy appeared to decrease as the number of affair partners increased-despite the total number of sexual encounters remaining constant across scenarios. In Experiment 2, we replicated this effect using a between-subjects design and found evidence for the potential mediating role of emotional attachment concerns. Participants in Experiment 2 also rated one-off encounters across multiple affair partners as "more" cheating than the same number of encounters in relation to a single affair partner, suggesting greater jealousy in response to "less" cheating. Importantly, anger at one's partner did not significantly differ across scenarios, indicating some degree of specificity to jealousy. These seemingly paradoxical findings support functional accounts of romantic jealousy and highlight the utility of adaptationist approaches to affective science. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved).

papers.title: Inhibition of the lipid peroxidation and glutathione peroxidase-like activity of 2-methyl benzoselenazoles.
papers.abstract: 2-Methyl benzoselenazoles were synthesized via the reaction of in situ-generated sodium selenolate with acetyl chloride at room temperature. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction confirmed a nearly planar structure due to non-bonding Se⋯O interactions, supported by computational analyses. All compounds exhibited good glutathione peroxidase-like antioxidant activity in a coupled reductase assay, as compared to the reference, ebselen. The most active compound was further evaluated under varying concentrations of glutathione to gain deeper insights into its catalytic efficiency. 77Se{1H} NMR mechanistic study was performed to provide evidence for the key intermediates involved in the decomposition of peroxide. The radical-trapping antioxidant activity of benzoselenazoles was evaluated by the inhibition of azo-initiated autoxidation of cumene in chlorobenzene. It showed peroxyl radical-trapping capability, with an inhibition constant of 1.4 × 103 M-1 s-1 and a stoichiometric factor (n) ≈ 2, due to H-atom transfer from the amide group, as further confirmed by theoretical calculations. In addition to their antioxidant activities, molecular dynamics studies revealed favourable binding interactions with vascular endothelial growth factor receptor-2 (VEGFR-2), suggesting dual antioxidant and anti-angiogenic roles.

papers.title: Cluster-Scale MoOx-IrO2 Heterointerfaces Steer Dual-Site Coupling and Interfacial Water Dynamics for Fast and Durable Oxygen Evolution.
papers.abstract: Proton exchange membrane water electrolyzers (PEMWEs) are central to renewable-powered green hydrogen production. As the benchmark electrocatalyst for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER), conventional single-phase IrO2 is constrained by linear scaling relations among oxygenated intermediates, compounded by severe mass-transport limitations and poorly regulated interfacial water structures. Here, we design a Turing-type MoOx-IrO2 heterostructure with strongly coupled cluster-scale interfaces, which enables dual-function Ir-Mo synergy that breaks fundamental kinetic limitations and optimizes interfacial water structures. At the reaction pathway level, Brønsted-acidic MoOx clusters promote water dissociation to generate reactive Mo─OH* intermediates, triggering radical coupling with adjacent Ir─O* species to form OOH* and thus circumventing the linear scaling relation. At the interfacial microenvironment level, MoOx reorganizes the rigid hydrogen-bonding networks and increases the population of free H2O species, effectively alleviating concentration overpotentials under high-current-density operation. When integrated into a practical 25 cm2 membrane electrode assembly, this catalyst delivers a PEMWE cell voltage of 1.71 V at 3 A cm-2 and an ultralow degradation rate of ∼9.5 µV h-1 over 1000 h, with a total platinum-group-metal loading of merely 0.5 mg cm-2 across both electrodes. Our dual-modulation strategy establishes a transformative paradigm for developing low-iridium and durable OER electrocatalysts toward practical green hydrogen production.

papers.title: Isolation of uranocenium, the bis-[8]annulene uranium cation.
papers.abstract: Uranocene, [UIV(η8-C8H8)2], is the actinide equivalent to ferrocene. While ferrocene is readily oxidised to the ferrocenium cation, higher oxidation states of uranocene are unknown. Here we report the elusive uranocenium cation, [UV(η8-C8H8)2]+, and demonstrate using electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy and magnetometry that this formal U(V) complex has a 5 f 1 ground state. Enhanced uranium 5 f and 6 d mixing into filled δ-symmetry bonding orbitals in uranocenium, compared to uranocene, amplifies interorbital electron-electron repulsion, and counteracts bond length contraction, which minimises structural change. This manifests in solution where the uranocene/uranocenium redox couple exhibits near-ideal electrochemical reversibility, and in the solid-state where X-ray diffraction studies show minimal U-C bond length change upon oxidation. This demonstrates a case where actinide covalency governs molecular structure and physical properties across both solid and solution phases.

papers.title: The role of cadherins and catenins in endometrial function and embryo implantation: A comprehensive review.
papers.abstract: Cadherins and catenins are essential transmembrane proteins and cytoplasmic binding partners that mediate cell-cell adhesion, intracellular signaling, and the maintenance of tissue architecture. Their coordinated functions are central to endometrial biology and embryo implantation, a process that requires complex cell-cell interactions and tissue remodeling for pregnancy to be established. In this review, we summarize current evidence on the molecular mechanisms through which cadherins and catenins regulate endometrial receptivity and support embryo attachment to maternal tissue. We also discuss how advances in molecular biology and reproductive medicine have clarified the roles of cadherin-catenin complexes in cell adhesion, intracellular signaling, including Wnt/β-catenin signaling, and the regulation of trophoblast invasion. In addition, we examine the potential clinical relevance of dysfunction in these complexes, which has been associated with implantation failure and infertility. A clearer understanding of cadherin-catenin function in the endometrium may support the development of diagnostic tools and therapeutic targets for infertility.

papers.title: Molecular Connectivity Controls Electronic Coupling and Charge-Transfer Dynamics at Anthracene-MoS2 Interfaces.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.abstract: Controlling interfacial charge-transfer (CT) interactions is a central challenge in two-dimensional (2D) organic-inorganic hybrid materials. Here, we show that molecular connectivity strongly governs excited-state evolution at a 2D heterointerface using anthracene (An) donors covalently attached to few-layer MoS2 nanosheets through an N-benzylsuccinimide linker at either the 2- or 9-position, generating two constitutional isomers, MoS2-2-An and MoS2-9-An. Ultrafast transient absorption spectroscopy reveals markedly different photodynamics that depend strongly on the donor attachment position. Photoexcitation of MoS2-2-An produces a long-lived interfacial CT excited state, whereas MoS2-9-An undergoes rapid formation of a full charge-separated state. The contrasting behavior is consistent with connectivity-controlled differences in donor orientation at the interface, which modulate orbital overlap and electronic coupling and may influence structural reorganization. Theoretical calculations further support that the more coplanar geometry of 2-An, exhibiting a calculated tilt angle (θ) of 29.5° relative to the MoS2 basal plane, enhances electronic coupling and stabilizes an intermediately coupled CT state, whereas the more upright 9-An orientation (θ = 42.1°) weakens orbital mixing and favors direct charge separation. These findings demonstrate that constitutional connectivity can serve as a molecular-level design parameter for tuning interfacial electronic coupling and directing excited-state evolution in 2D hybrid heterostructures relevant to optoelectronics, photocatalysis, and solar-energy conversion.

papers.title: Dark-State-Mediated Low-Energy Electron Attachment to Molecular Oxygen: Symmetry Adapted Decomposition of the DEA Resonance through Dyson-Orbitals' Incoherent Mixing.
papers.journal: The journal of physical chemistry letters
papers.abstract: Dissociative electron attachment (DEA) to O2 exhibits a prominent resonance peak at ∼6.5 eV, producing O- with a single kinetic energy band (∼1.5 eV) and a distinct four-lobed angular distribution. Using velocity-map imaging and complex absorbing potential equation-of-motion electron-attachment coupled-cluster singles and doubles (CAP-EOM-EA-CCSD) calculations, we notice that this resonance is mediated by electron-impact excitation to the optically dark a1Δg and b1Σg+ states, which suggests electron impact excitation to these optically dark excited states provides an appropriate electronic structure for electron attachment forming 2Πu, 2Πg and 2,4Σu Feshbach resonances. The measured angular distribution is reproduced by an incoherent superposition of three symmetry channels: 2Πu (66.5%); 2Πg (25.1%); and 2,4Σu (8.5%). The Dyson orbitals computed from the CAP-EOM-EA-CCSD calculations quantitatively reproduce the channel weights and their energy dependencies. This dark-state-mediated mechanism pinpointedly resolves the experimental observations and provides a general symmetry-adapted framework for decomposing DEA resonances from the fragmented anions angular distributions.

papers.title: Molecular structure dependence of thermo-diffusion in binary mixture using thermal Lens spectroscopy.
papers.journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Thermo-diffusion (Soret effect) in binary mixtures arises from the coupling of heat and mass fluxes in an inhomogeneous temperature field. In this work, we investigated how molecular structural isomerism influences thermo-diffusion in binary mixtures of butanol isomers (n-, s-, i-, and t-BuOH) with carbon tetrachloride (CCl4) using femtosecond laser-induced thermal lens spectroscopy (FTLS). The thermal lens (TL) response of the mixtures reflected the interplay between heat conduction and mass transport, which evolved systematically with composition. The magnitude and sign of the Soret coefficient exhibited pronounced nonlinear dependence on composition and showed distinct sign changes at characteristic concentrations, occurring at ∼50% and ∼ 40% CCl4 for n-BuOH and s-BuOH systems and at ∼70% CCl4 for i-BuOH and t-BuOH mixtures. These findings indicate that thermo-diffusion in non-ideal mixtures is governed by molecular structure and intermolecular interactions rather than by bulk transport properties. Furthermore, FTLS is a highly sensitive technique for probing coupled heat-mass transport processes.

papers.title: A dianionic allene bound to vanadium(iii) enables interconversion between vanadatetrahedranes, vanadacyclobutadienes and deprotiovanadacyclobutadienes.
papers.abstract: Herein we disclose a novel route to redox-active vanadacyclobutadiene (VCBD) and vanadatetrahedrane (VTd) complexes, which circumvents a vanadium alkylidyne precursor ([VV][triple bond, length as m-dash]CR). [VV] VCBD salts and VTd's are prepared through an unusual, non-classical oxidative addition reaction via the addition of electrophiles to a low-spin [VIII] deprotiovanadacyclobutadiene (dVCBD). The microscopic reverse reaction, a reductive elimination, reverts the [VV] VCBD and VTd scaffolds back to the low-spin [VIII] dVCBD species via the addition of a Brønsted base. The interconversion of the [VV] VCBD salts and VTd's is mediated through anion exchange, which promotes a change in the spin-state and geometry of the organometallic species, highlighting the redox active nature of the allene ligand (C3) bound to vanadium (V). Single electron reduction of the [VV] VCBD or VTd with cobaltocene (CoCp2) led to the formation of neutral and radical-based [VIV] VCBDs. Oxidation of the [VIV] VCBDs with ferrocenium based salts ([FeCp2][X], X = BArF20 -, BArF24 -, OTf-) or chloride-delivering oxidants (i.e. triphenylmethyl chloride (Ph3CCl) or lead(ii) chloride (PbCl2)) regenerates the discrete [VV] VCBD salts or VTd's, respectively. Cyclic voltammetry studies reveal quasi-reversible one electron redox couples, while X-band electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectroscopic studies confirms the presence of a paramagnetic [VIV], d1 system in the VCBD. Computational analysis of the dVCBD, VTd, and VCBD complexes affords detailed insight into the structure and bonding of this unusual class of molecules and delineates the role of the anion in their interconversion. Further examination of the reaction of dVCBD with electrophiles corroborates the nonclassical character of the oxidative addition sequence involving metal-ligand cooperation, with ligand-centered redox activity, rather than a formal two-electron oxidation at the metal center. The present work demonstrates how

papers.title: Supporting meaningful contributions of people affected by Parkinson's throughout the research process: Key considerations for inclusive patient and public involvement across the globe.
papers.abstract: Patient and public involvement (PPI), defined as research undertaken with people affected by a condition as partners rather than participants, is increasingly recognized as a marker of high-quality research and is now encouraged or required by many funders. Research agendas and practices need to reflect the realities of people living with Parkinson's Disease (PD) ensuring research addresses the priorities of those affected.This narrative review examines the role of PPI across the research cycle, including priority setting, commissioning, study design, delivery, dissemination, implementation, and evaluation. We provide guidance and practical examples of how meaningful PPI can be achieved in PD research. The review explains how perspectives of lived experience can improve the relevance, feasibility, accessibility, and highlight its impact on PD research. We discuss practical considerations for embedding meaningful PPI, including project governance structures, dedicated staffing, remuneration, flexibility in conduct, and how to embed the perspectives of under-served PD communities in PPI. Finally, we consider challenges and opportunities for PPI in low- and middle-income countries, where underdiagnosis, stigma, health literacy barriers, and structural inequities require culturally responsive and community-led approaches.Involving people affected by Parkinson's as equal partners in research has the potential to improve individual studies and to reshape the wider PD research agenda to be more inclusive, representative, and responsive to the priorities of those most affected.To realise this potential, we must make a collective commitment to treat PPI as a requirement, provide funding and infrastructure support for implementation, and share experiences. papers.title: Positive Metacognition, Family Avoidance of Cancer Communication, and Psychological Distress in Breast Cancer Patients and Their Spouses: A Longitudinal Actor-Partner Interdependence Model.
papers.abstract: AIM: To examine longitudinal changes in positive metacognition and meta-emotion, family avoidance of cancer communication (FACC), and psychological distress in breast cancer patients and their spouses, and to test the mediating and cross-partner effects of FACC. METHODS: 265 patient-spouse dyads were recruited by convenience sampling from a tertiary hospital between January and December 2025, and 230 dyads completing all three assessments were analysed. The Positive Metacognitions and Positive Meta-Emotions Questionnaire, the Family Avoidance of Communication about Cancer scale, and the 10-item Kessler Psychological Distress Scale were administered at baseline (T1, within 1 week after surgery), 6 weeks (T2) and 12 weeks (T3) postoperatively; follow-up was completed in March 2026. Repeated-measures ANOVA and a cross-lagged actor-partner interdependence mediation model were used. RESULTS: PMCEQ scores increased while FACC and K10 scores decreased over time in both partners (all P < 0.001). FACC significantly mediated the PMCEQ-K10 association in patients (β = 0.037, P < 0.001) and spouses (β = 0.016, P < 0.01); because higher PMCEQ predicted less avoidance and more avoidance predicted greater distress, these coefficients denote protective indirect associations (higher PMCEQ → lower avoidance → lower distress). Partner effects were also significant (patient PMCEQ → spouse FACC → spouse K10, β = 0.019, P < 0.05; spouse PMCEQ → patient FACC → patient K10, β = 0.040, P < 0.001). Distress showed positive dyadic spillover (β = 0.21-0.25, P < 0.001), indicating that higher distress in one partner predicted higher subsequent distress in the other. CONCLUSIONS: In marital dyads, positive metacognition and meta-emotion increased while avoidance communication and distress declined across the early postoperative period. papers.title: Dyadic Coping with Dyspnoea-Related Kinesiophobia in Couples Living with COPD: "Entrapped Together or Moving Through Together" - A Constructivist Grounded Theory.
papers.journal: International journal of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
papers.abstract: AIM: To generate a theory explaining how patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and their partners experience and navigate the process of coping with dyspnoea-related kinesiophobia within everyday pulmonary rehabilitation and home-based disease management. METHODS: A qualitative study using constructivist grounded theory was conducted in the respiratory department of one large tertiary hospital and its affiliated community health service centre in Shanxi Province, China. Initial purposive sampling and subsequent theoretical sampling were used to recruit 21 couples, comprising clinically stable patients with COPD and kinesiophobia (operationally defined as Breathlessness Beliefs Questionnaire-Activity Avoidance subscale score >6) and their cohabiting partners. Data were collected through face-to-face dyadic interviews. Concurrent data analysis employed a constant comparative approach, facilitated by NVivo 12 software, to iteratively refine emerging codes and categories. RESULTS: The 21 patients represented GOLD airflow limitation grades 1-3, including grade 1 (n=2), grade 2 (n=12), and grade 3 (n=7). Analysis generated the core category "Entrapped Together or Moving Through Together", which conceptualises kinesiophobia as a dynamic dyadic process rather than solely an individual experience. Patients' symptom-related fear entered couple interactions through two distinct patterns: patients' expressions of distress elicited kinesiophobia and protective anxiety in partners, whereas partners' protective monitoring and restriction could become incorporated into patients' movement-related concerns. Couples subsequently responded through four patterns-joint avoidance, motivational conflict, support mismatch, and the paradox of love. papers.title: Actor-Partner Effects on Dyadic Adjustment, Relationship Satisfaction, and Well-Being after Spinal Cord Injury.
papers.journal: The American journal of occupational therapy : official publication of the American Occupational Therapy Association
papers.abstract: ImportanceSpinal cord injury (SCI) extends beyond the injured individual to intimate partners, often altering shared occupations, relational roles, and well-being. Understanding dyadic processes is critical for occupational therapy practice.ObjectiveTo examine associations among dyadic adjustment, relationship satisfaction, and well-being in SCI dyads using an actor-partner interdependence model.DesignCross-sectional dyadic study using baseline data from an intervention trial (SupportGroove).SettingHealth care institutions and community-based settings.ParticipantsEighty-two community-dwelling SCI-partner dyads (164 adults; mean ages: SCI, 50.1 ± 15.7; partners, 48.5 ± 14.5 years), 3 months to 5 years postinjury.Outcomes and MeasuresSelf-report; Revised Dyadic Adjustment Scale, Couples Satisfaction Index-4, and Neuro-QoL Positive Affect and Well-Being.ResultsDyadic adjustment was significantly and positively associated with relationship satisfaction among SCI participants (β = 0.66, standard error [SE] = 0.09, p < .001), indicating a large effect. A similar significant positive association was observed among partners (β = 0.47, SE = 0.11, p < .001), reflecting a medium effect size. Additionally, partners' relationship satisfaction was significantly and positively related to their own well-being (β = 0.35, SE = 0.14, p = .010), with a medium effect. papers.title: The Raine Study: a multigenerational Western Australian birth and life-course cohort advancing research on the developmental origins of health and disease.
papers.journal: Journal of developmental origins of health and disease
papers.abstract: The Developmental Origins of Health and Disease (DOHaD) framework has transformed understanding of how early-life exposures shape health across the life course, yet populations from Oceania remain underrepresented in this research. The Raine Study is a globally unique, multigenerational longitudinal pregnancy cohort established in Western Australia, one of the world's most geographically isolated regions. The study recruited 2900 pregnant women (Generation1) in 1989, which resulted in 2868 live births forming Generation 2, and is now currently recruiting Generation 3 (the children of Generation 2). This paper describes the evolution of the Raine Study from its origins as a pregnancy cohort grounded in DOHaD to a comprehensive life-course and multigenerational research resource. This resource has led to key research findings that have informed international clinical guidelines and national and state health policies across areas including prenatal development and care safety, neurodevelopment, cardiometabolic health, obesity, liver disease, physical activity, mental health, sedentary behaviour, sleep, and assisted reproductive technologies. Central to the Raine Study's success is a longstanding commitment to participant partnership and engagement, resulting in exceptional retention and strong consumer involvement in governance and research prioritisation. The Raine Study demonstrates the critical value of well-characterised, place-based cohorts for advancing DOHaD and life-course science and provides a globally significant resource to inform prevention strategies, precision medicine, and public health policy across generations.

papers.title: Meeting report of the fifth symposium organized by the coalition to strengthen the HPV immunization community (CHIC): Nairobi, Kenya - advancing sustainable HPV vaccination programs in Africa.
papers.abstract: HPV vaccination coverage across Africa has improved substantially in recent years but remains below elimination thresholds, with persistent gaps in reaching hard-to-reach populations and growing uncertainty around future financing. This report summarizes proceedings from the fifth regional symposium of the Coalition to Strengthen the HPV Immunization Community (CHIC), held in Nairobi, Kenya, in October 2025 in collaboration with Kenya's Ministry of Health. The three-day symposium convened over 100 participants from 22 African countries, including national immunisation program managers, ministry officials, researchers, civil society representatives, and global partners (WHO, UNICEF, Gavi, PATH, the Gates Foundation). The agenda, developed through stakeholder interviews and prior scientific and advisory input, centered on six subthemes related to program sustainability. Plenary sessions addressed epidemiological trends, national policy updates including Kenya's transition to a single-dose schedule, and implications of Gavi's upcoming consolidated funding model (Gavi 6.0). Country snapshot presentations and service-delivery case studies facilitated cross-country peer learning. On day three, though an electronic poll of helped to prioritize 12 candidate implementation themes, which structured subsequent round table working groups. Countries then developed individual action plans identifying priority challenges, responsible stakeholders, and implementation timelines. Sustainable service delivery, financing, and data systems emerged as the highest-priority implementation themes. Country action plans most frequently targeted data systems strengthening, communication and community engagement, sustainable service delivery, and financing mechanisms, with additional attention to service integration, hard-to-reach populations, and target population expansion. Cross-cutting synthesis identified recurring concerns regarding HPV vaccination for people living with HIV, fragmented d

papers.title: From productive coupling to catalytic commitment: An evolutionarily tuned interdomain connector in Leishmania Aha1 orchestrates Hsp90 activation.
papers.abstract: Hsp90 activation depends on cochaperones that couple binding to catalytic commitment, yet some structural elements mediating this transition remain poorly understood. Here, we investigate the molecular mechanism by which the cochaperone Aha1 from Leishmania braziliensis activates Hsp90 and present evidence supporting a linker-mediated disorder-to-order transition associated with this process. Thermodynamic analyses show that, while the Aha1 N-domain mediates Hsp90 binding, only the full-length Aha1 containing its wild-type interdomain linker exhibits a distinct enthalpy-dominated interaction and robust ATPase stimulation. Structural and kinetic measurements indicate that the wild-type linker modulates the conformational distribution of the Aha1 N-domain, promoting productive docking with Hsp90. Structural modeling suggests that the Aha1 linker adopts an α-helical conformation in the activated complex, whereas the corresponding synthetic linker peptide displays inducible helicity under structure-promoting conditions, consistent with a binding-coupled disorder-to-order transition. This transition appears evolutionarily tuned, as linker properties vary across species. Collectively, these findings support a model in which the Aha1 linker actively couples binding to activation, providing a new framework for Hsp90 regulation and highlighting a potential target for selective intervention in protozoan Aha1:Hsp90 systems.

papers.title: Feasibility of a Co-Designed Personalized Cognitive Reablement Program Delivered via Digital Voice Assistants for Older Adults Living With Early-Stage Dementia or Mild Cognitive Impairment: Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Home-based reablement programs have improved everyday functioning for people living with early-stage dementia or mild cognitive impairment (MCI), but the substantial time commitment required for delivery by health professionals has created a barrier to widespread implementation. Digital technology could facilitate delivery, but traditional devices such as smartphones and tablets present usability challenges for this population. We have co-designed a cognitive reablement program, VOICE-COG, that can deliver personalized interventions broadcast via voice-controlled digital voice assistants (DVAs). OBJECTIVE: This pilot nonblinded randomized controlled trial examined the feasibility and potential effectiveness of VOICE-COG for older adults living with dementia or MCI to guide the design of a full-scale trial. METHODS: Older adults (aged 60-85 years) with a self-reported diagnosis of dementia or MCI (N=30) were recruited via Facebook or the StepUp-for Dementia Research database and randomized to either a DVA intervention (n=15) or control (n=15) group for 12 weeks. Each participant randomized to the intervention group and their care partner met with a psychologist via Zoom to select 2 or 3 personalized goals from the VOICE-COG program. The personalized program was input into the software (BuddyLink) by researchers for broadcast via a DVA (Amazon Alexa Show 8). Participants in the control group received enhanced usual care, consisting of treatment as usual, plus weekly informational emails. Primary feasibility outcomes were recruitment, retention, device-recorded adherence, and the System Usability Scale (SUS). Secondary outcomes were self-reported by the participant and care partner via web-based Qualtrics forms and included the Goal Attainment Scale-Light (GAS), changes in participant mood, cognition, and everyday functioning, and carer burden. RESULTS: The recruitment rate was 86% (30/35) and the retention rate was 97% (29/30), with 1 participant in the in

papers.title: Analysing the implementation and transferability of an enhanced care pathway integrating systematic supportive cancer care and patient-partner support for people living with anal cancer: Protocol for a mixed-methods study in two French cancer centres.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Supportive cancer care (SCC) is essential for comprehensive oncology care. It addresses treatment-related adverse effects, reduces long-term sequelae and improves patients' quality of life. Patient-partner (PP) programmes positively impact psychological well-being, patient empowerment and supportive care. Nevertheless, access to SCC remains inconsistent, fragmented and unequally distributed, while PPs are rarely integrated into routine cancer care pathways. Anal cancer is a predominantly localised cancer with high survival rates. Treatment is associated with acute toxicity and often severe long-term sequelae. This interventional public health research study aims to implement and evaluate an innovative enhanced care pathway combining systematic SCC and structured PP support for all individuals diagnosed with anal cancer living in France. The study will assess the intervention's clinical, organisational, and social effects, and will identify the conditions required for its long-term sustainability and transferability. METHODS AND DESIGN: This is a longitudinal mixed-methods case study conducted in two French Comprehensive Cancer Centres. The intervention entails introducing a systematic, coordinated, and repeated SCC offer together with a structured PP support programme for all patients diagnosed with anal cancer and over 12 months following diagnosis. One centre will implement the enhanced care pathway, while the other will initially provide standard care before progressively adopting the intervention during the transferability phase. Quantitative data will include patient-reported outcomes, clinical information and implementation indicators. Qualitative data exploring implementation processes, organisational changes and contextual determinants, will be collected through observations, semi-structured interviews, focus groups and PP activity logs. DISCUSSION: The study's results will provide essential scientific knowledge on the implementation of programme

papers.title: Say Less! Backchanneling and HPA-axis Attunement, But Not Semantic Synchrony, Relate to Couples' Relationship Quality Across the Transition to Parenthood.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Language and physiology each carry information about how couples attune, yet are rarely studied together, especially during vulnerable periods such as the transition to parenthood. Semantic synchrony, or shared meaning across partners' speaking turns, is a potential marker of relational functioning that may reflect couples' use of active listening and reflection to validate one another's concerns. Semantic synchrony may also intersect with other dimensions of health-relevant synchrony such as covariation in partners' hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis. METHODS: The present study examined semantic and HPA-axis/cortisol synchrony in 100 expectant parent dyads during lab-based discussions in pregnancy and at six months postpartum. Results: Semantic synchrony was present across all conversations and was strongest during discussions of conflict. Positive HPA-axis synchrony emerged at both timepoints, but semantic and HPA-axis synchrony were unrelated. Semantic synchrony during discussions about relationship conflict was negatively associated with partners' validation of one another (i.e., communicating sincere understanding), but this association was primarily attributable to couples' backchanneling (e.g., "mmhm," "uh-huh") - brief verbal expressions that communicate understanding without interrupting the speaker. Neither form of synchrony predicted relationship quality at either visit, with one exception: postpartum HPA-axis synchrony marginally predicted couples' relationship quality (P=.04). Moreover, partners' backchanneling during discussions of conflict was positively associated with participants' relationship quality. CONCLUSIONS: Together, these findings suggest that it is backchanneling, not semantic synchrony, that is associated with greater validation and relationship quality and may therefore serve as a potential linguistic marker of relational functioning.

papers.title: Cytoskeletal and Extracellular Factors Regulating Stem Cell Differentiation: Mechanisms, Tools, and Emerging Applications.
papers.abstract: Stem cell lineage determination is governed not only by biochemical cues but also by the organization and force-generating state of the cytoskeleton, which integrates extracellular mechanical cues into transcriptional and epigenetic responses. Cytoskeletal organization and remodeling play essential roles in stem cell fate determination, as well as other relevant biological processes including development, tissue regeneration, and disease progression. In this review, we first outline the different types of cytoskeletal structures-actin filaments, microtubules, and intermediate filaments-and their coordinated roles in cell shape, polarity, and contractility. We then discuss how extracellular cues, including matrix stiffness, geometry, topography, shear, stretch, and compression remodel cytoskeletal distribution and adhesion dynamics to affect stem cell lineage commitment. We highlight matrix viscoelasticity and stress relaxation as time-dependent mechanical regulators that modulate traction transmission, focal adhesion, and cytoskeletal tension, thereby directing stem cell differentiation outcomes beyond stiffness alone. We next discuss mechanotransduction pathways, such as RhoA/ROCK-mediated contractility, Wnt/β-catenin, Piezo1/Piezo2, and YAP/TAZ nuclear shuttling, which couple cytoskeletal forces to gene regulation. We further summarize quantitative approaches to measure cell molecular forces, including traction force microscopy, molecular tension sensors, and advanced live-cell imaging platforms. Finally, we discuss the translational potential of cytoskeleton-informed design principles in regenerative medicine, where they can be leveraged to improve stem cell biomanufacturing, optimize tunable biomaterials, and develop more predictive mechanopathology models. Together, these developments will establish cytoskeletal organization as a controllable, engineerable lever for directing stem cell fate and enabling functional tissue formation.

papers.title: Unpacking behavioral and organizational enablers of blockchain adoption: A hybrid PLS-ANN-fsQCA investigation.
papers.abstract: Blockchain technology has ushered as a transformative force, offering enhanced transparency, security and traceability across supply chains. Despite its potential, blockchain adoption in supply chain finance remains limited. This study integrates the Technology-Organization-Environment framework with key constructs from the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology to identify behavioral drivers of blockchain adoption. It captures technological, organizational, and environmental influences alongside individual beliefs related to usefulness and ease of use, offering a multi-dimensional view of adoption behavior in supply chain finance. Data from 238 supply chain professionals were analyzed using an integrated approach combining Structural Equation Modelling, Artificial Neural Network technique and Fuzzy-set Qualitative Comparative Analysis. The findings indicate that top management and trading partner support are the most influential predictors, followed by organizational readiness, technology maturity, and performance expectancy. Meanwhile, relative advantage, competitive pressure, and effort expectancy exert no significant influence. By integrating two mutually reinforcing theories, validated through a multi-method analytical approach, this study offers the first multi-dimensional assessment of blockchain adoption in India's supply chain finance context, providing actionable insights for strategic alignment and policy formulation to facilitate wider diffusion.

papers.title: [Joint experience of Spain and the WHO in advancing the Acceleration Plan to End childhood Obesity].
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Obesity is one of the most pressing global health challenges, affecting over one billion people worldwide. Despite extensive evidence on effective interventions, implementation has been inconsistent across countries. In response, the World Health Organization (WHO) launched the Acceleration Plan to Stop Obesity in 2022 to catalyze coordinated, measurable, and sustainable action. This article examined the joint experiences of Spain and WHO in advancing the Acceleration Plan, focusing on the international context, Spain's engagement and leadership, and the shared schedule of actions. It also provides a critical reflection on the strengths and weaknesses of the Acceleration Plan and the collaboration. METHODS: A descriptive policy analysis was conducted based on WHO documentation, Spain's national policy announcements, and the programmatic architecture of the Acceleration Plan. The analysis highlights governance mechanisms, political processes, and implementation pathways. RESULTS: Spain's joining of to the Acceleration Plan in 2024 marked a pivotal moment, reinforcing the global governance architecture through its leadership in launching and steering the WHO Accountability Series. Joint actions include preparations for the first High-Level Political Summit on Obesity to be hosted by Spain in 2026, annual ministerial engagements, and technical cooperation to monitor progress across countries. Spain's multisectoral policies provide practical examples of implementation aligned with WHO recommendations. CONCLUSIONS: The Spain-WHO partnership demonstrates how national leadership, political convening power, and structured accountability can accelerate progress on obesity prevention and management. However, challenges persist, including heterogeneous country capacities, data limitations, and risks to sustained political commitment. Continued multilevel coordination will be essential for achieving the 2030 targets. OBJECTIVE: La obesidad constituye uno de los princ

papers.title: Single-cell mapping of human plasma cell fate reveals a commitment checkpoint and Cav-1β expression associated with mTORC1 machinery.
papers.abstract: Human B cell differentiation into antibody-secreting plasma cells (PCs) requires coordinated transcriptional and organelle remodeling. Using single-cell transcriptomics in an in vitro human B cell differentiation system, we identified a Day-8 commitment checkpoint separating PC, memory B cell, and germinal center-like trajectories and defined an XBP1-associated transcriptional program linked to organelle remodeling. Within this program, CAV1 was induced during PC commitment and encoded a non-caveolar Cav-1β isoform expressed in plasmablasts and PCs. Proteomic analyses showed that Cav-1β associates with endoplasmic reticulum, secretory, and nutrient-sensing proteins, including components of the V-ATPase-RAGulator-RAG complex. CAV1 silencing had modest effects on PC differentiation but did not alter acute mTORC1 activation or antibody secretion. These findings place Cav-1β within the membrane and organelle remodeling program of human PCs and highlight how intracellular architecture may be coupled to metabolic and secretory adaptation during plasma cell differentiation.

papers.title: How to tackle inequities in bereavement support for ethnically diverse communities: a national qualitative study using experience-based co-design.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: High-income countries globally are becoming increasingly diverse. People from ethnically diverse communities experience inequities in accessing bereavement support, but evidence to inform equitable provision remains limited. We aimed to determine how formal bereavement support services can better serve ethnically diverse communities by identifying barriers to and facilitators of equitable access, defining key components of culturally safe and appropriate bereavement care, and developing a logic model and recommendations for equitable bereavement support. METHODS: Multi-phase national qualitative study, drawing on experience-based co-design principles. We conducted interviews (n = 53) and focus groups (n = 9) with 121 bereaved people from 13 ethnically diverse backgrounds, interviews with 23 bereavement support providers across 12 services, four online co-design workshops with bereaved people and stakeholders (n = 53), and a hybrid workshop to refine recommendations (n = 29 stakeholders). Recruitment and data collection prioritised cultural safety and an asset-based approach. Directed thematic analysis was informed by Levesque et al.'s access to healthcare framework. RESULTS: Barriers to equitable bereavement support arose across the access pathway but were concentrated mainly within bereavement support organisations and the wider bereavement support system. Racism and intersectionality were cross-cutting themes, influencing whether bereaved people could identify, trust, reach and engage with support. Key barriers included poor signposting and referral, long waiting lists, limited staff diversity, language barriers, weak organisational commitment to equity, precarious funding, and white-centred, individualised models of grief support. Participants identified culturally safe and equitable care as requiring anti-racist practice, sustained community partnership, provision of support in trusted settings

papers.title: Generation of Spontaneously Beating Neuromyocardial Organoids with Neural Crest-Derived Proprioceptive-Biased Neurons and Real-Time Respirometry.
papers.abstract: The neural crest gives rise to diverse cell types, including the proprioceptive sensory neurons that relay limb and organ position to the central nervous system. Studying how these neurons interact with their peripheral targets in a human context has been constrained by the lack of integrated in vitro models that combine neural crest derivatives with functional effector tissue. Here, we present a protocol for generating spontaneously beating neuromyocardial organoids from human pluripotent stem cells (hPSCs), incorporating neural crest-derived proprioceptive-biased neurons. Differentiation proceeds under defined conditions that reproducibly co-specify cardiac and neural crest lineages, yielding organoids that contract rhythmically within 7-8 days and harbor proprioceptive-biased sensory neuron populations. We further describe how to integrate these organoids with continuous oxygen consumption rate (OCR) monitoring, enabling non-invasive measurement of mitochondrial respiration over days to weeks. This longitudinal readout captures dynamic shifts in respiration that are inaccessible to endpoint assays, providing a sensitive functional metric of metabolic health and stress. The combined model is broadly applicable to questions in human cardiac and neural crest development, neuromuscular and sensorimotor integration, and the metabolic basis of disease. We illustrate its utility in Friedreich's ataxia (FRDA), a mitochondrial disorder affecting both proprioceptive neurons and cardiac tissue, in which real-time OCR monitoring reveals respiratory deficits. The protocol offers a reproducible, scalable system for interrogating neural crest biology alongside cardiac function and for evaluating metabolic phenotypes and pharmacological interventions in a physiologically relevant, multi-lineage human context. Notably, the entire differentiation sequence runs on chemically defined, animal-free media, and organoids form directly in standard U-bottom 96-well plates, without ultra-l

papers.title: Adaptive and Multicolored Electrochromic Smart Window with Transparent-Opaque Switchable Radiative Cooling.
papers.abstract: Transparent radiative-cooling windows can reduce cooling demand while preserving daylighting, yet high solar transmission becomes undesirable under strong solar irradiation. Although existing electrochromic windows can regulate solar transmittance, simultaneously achieving strong solar rejection, radiative heat dissipation, and wide-gamut coloration remains challenging. Here, we develop dynamic colorful radiative cooling windows by integrating planar coupled nanocavities with reversible silver electrodeposition. Electrochemically controlled Ag deposition/stripping reconfigures Fabry-Pérot resonances, enabling reversible switching between colored transparent and highly reflective colored opaque states while retaining high mid-infrared emissivity. The devices can achieve >40% modulation in average visible transmittance and cover 99.5% of the sRGB color gamut. Under outdoor conditions, they exhibit temperature drops of ∼7.0 °C compared to conventional glass and ∼8.7 °C relative to commercial electrochromic glass. This work provides a versatile platform for dynamic optical regulation with diverse requirements, paving the way for next-generation multifunctional smart windows, building envelopes, and smart photonic devices.

papers.title: Tailored Graphene Oxide Incorporated PES/CA Mixed-Matrix Loose Nanofiltration Membranes for Water Softening and Divalent Salt Removal.
papers.journal: Water environment research : a research publication of the Water Environment Federation
papers.abstract: Achieving a simultaneous enhancement of permeability and selectivity remains a central challenge in nanofiltration membrane design. Here, we report the fabrication of high-performance polyether sulfone-cellulose acetate (PES/CA) mixed-matrix membranes via phase inversion, employing polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP) as a pore-forming agent and graphene oxide (GO) as a hydrophilic nanofiller to precisely tailor membrane structure and transport behavior. Systematic characterization using SEM, FTIR, and physicochemical analyses reveals that PVP induces the formation of interconnected finger-like channels and macrovoids, whereas GO incorporation significantly enhances surface hydrophilicity and interfacial compatibility within the polymer matrix. An optimal GO loading of 1.5 wt.% enables uniform dispersion, maximizing wettability and transport efficiency; in contrast, higher loading (2 wt.%) leads to nanosheet agglomeration, reduced hydrophilicity, and restricted permeation pathways. The synergistic interplay between PVP-induced porosity and GO-enhanced surface functionality results in a finely tuned membrane architecture that alleviates the conventional permeability-selectivity trade-off. The optimized membrane exhibits a stable pure water flux of 95 L m-2 h-1, coupled with improved salt rejection efficiencies of 46% (NaCl), 75% (MgCl2), and 59% (Na2SO4), significantly outperforming pristine PES/CA membranes. These findings demonstrate a scalable and effective strategy for designing loose nanofiltration membranes, offering promising potential for energy-efficient water softening and divalent salt removal from brackish water.

papers.title: Pressure and Cross-Flow Dependent Interfacial Fouling of Mesoporous PES-PUMA Membranes During Water-in-Oil Emulsion Separation.
papers.abstract: Water-in-oil (W/O) emulsion treatment is challenging because efficient membrane separation requires simultaneous control of oil transport, water rejection, interfacial interactions, and fouling resistance. However, the coupled effects of operating pressure and cross-flow hydrodynamics on membrane pore accessibility, foulant-layer evolution, and the permeability-rejection trade-off during cyclic W/O emulsion treatment remain insufficiently understood. In this study, an electrospun mesoporous polyurethane-melamine/polyethersulfone (PES-PUMA) membrane was evaluated for the separation of stabilized W/O emulsions under different operating pressures and feed flow rates. At an ultra-low pressure of 20 kPa, the membrane achieved an oil permeate flux of 36.5 ± 2.7 L m-2 h-1 and water rejection of 93.1 ± 2.1%. Increasing the operating pressure to 100 kPa increased the oil permeate flux to 87.6 ± 3.5 L m-2 h-1 while decreasing water rejection to 78.2 ± 1.8%. Increasing the cross-flow rate from 0.05 to 0.5 mL s-1 increased the oil permeate flux from 23.4 ± 0.7 to 90.7 ± 2.1 L m-2 h-1 while decreasing water rejection from 95.3 ± 2.1% to 78.4 ± 1.2%. Quadratic regression models revealed significant nonlinear relationships between hydraulic operating conditions and both separation responses, providing a quantitative description of the pressure- and flow-dependent performance trade-off. Higher cross-flow reduced foulant-layer thickness and favored more reversible fouling, whereas increasing operating pressure promoted pore constriction and compact foulant deposition. These findings establish a quantitative pressure-cross-flow-transport-fouling relationship, demonstrating that hydraulic conditions jointly regulate membrane permeability, water rejection, foulant-layer development, and fouling reversibility. This study therefore provides mechanistic and quantitative insight into optimizing the operation of the established PES-PUMA membrane to ba

papers.title: HIV-related stigma among people living with HIV in metropolitan and regional areas of New South Wales, Australia.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: This exploratory study aimed to investigate differences between metropolitan and regional people living with HIV (PLHIV) in relation to experiences of stigma and openness about HIV status. METHODS: PLHIV attending publicly funded sexual health services in metropolitan Sydney or regional NSW completed an anonymous, cross-sectional survey about experiences of HIV-related stigma in the past year. Multivariable logistic regression analysis identified differences between metropolitan and regional participants. RESULTS: Among 89 participants, 79.8% (n = 71) were from metropolitan Sydney and 20.2% (n = 18) were from regional NSW. Approximately 50% of both groups reported any past-year experience of HIV-related stigma. Multivariable analysis found that regional participants were older than metropolitan participants (aOR 2.26, 95% CI: 1.18-4.32), were less likely to report sexual or intimate partner rejection (aOR 0.11, 95% CI: 0.02-0.64) and were more likely to report any past-year stigma from doctors (aOR 5.57, 95% CI: 1.05-29.66). CONCLUSIONS: Although similar proportions of regional and metropolitan participants experienced HIV-related stigma, results suggest that these experiences were contextually different. Initiatives to reduce stigma and promote healthcare engagement among PLHIV may benefit from considering demographic differences and regional contexts (including healthcare settings). Opportunities may also exist to expand sexual health services (e.g. telehealth) to alleviate concerns about disclosing HIV status in smaller communities.
